title: DUF6383-domain containing protein from  Parabacteroides distasonis  predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《DUF6383-domain containing protein from  Parabacteroides distasonis  predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0001-p5】Here, we analyzed quantitative TMT-based metaproteomics of fecal samples from controls, patients with AUD, and AH, focusing on the bacterial metaproteome. Our aim was to identify a microbial protein signature of patients with ALD and to identify a biomarker.

【Introduction · s0001-p1】Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a major cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, ranging from benign hepatic steatosis to alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH), which 10–20% of patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD) develop. 1-4 AH is marked by an acute onset of jaundice after heavy and chronic alcohol use. 5 Patients frequently develop infections, systemic inflammatory response syndrome, and renal failure, which influences 90-day mortality. 6 Short-term survival is low with rates of 69–81.5% at day 28 and 62.5–69.1% at day 90. 7-10

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《DUF6383-domain containing protein from  Parabacteroides distasonis  predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Metaproteomics cohort: · s0002-s2001-s3001-p1】Details of this cohort have been reported. 18 , 20-23 Participants with AH were enrolled between June 2014 and May 2017 as part of a prospective, international, multicenter study conducted across eleven hospitals spanning five global regions (Integrated Approaches for Identifying Molecular Targets in Alcoholic Hepatitis (InTeam) Consortium, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02075918). We selected 80 patients with AH to include in our analysis, accompanied by 20 patients with AUD and 19 controls. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of the AH cohort are summarized in Table 1.

【Metaproteomics cohort: · s0002-s2001-s3001-p2】Diagnosis of AH was based on self-reported active alcohol abuse in the last three months (>50 g/day for men and >40 g/day for women) and clinical presentation. If clinically indicated, a liver biopsy was performed. Further eligibility criteria were biochemical features of liver injury with aspartate amino transferase (AST) exceeding alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and total serum bilirubin levels greater than 3 mg/dl in the last three months. Patients were excluded if they had evidence of autoimmune liver disease (ANA > 1/320), chronic viral hepatitis, hepatocellular carcinoma, complete portal vein thrombosis, extrahepatic terminal disease, or pregnancy.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《DUF6383-domain containing protein from  Parabacteroides distasonis  predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Validation of DUF6383 domain-containing protein as a marker for disease severity · s0003-s2006-p1】Since the levels of DUF6383 domain-containing protein increased with disease severity across the different stages, and a significant correlation was found with survival of patients with AH, we validated the correlation between DUF6383 domain-containing proteins and survival in an independent cohort. We used 72 samples from patients with AH enrolled in a multicenter cohort through the AlcHepNet consortium (Table 2), isolated DNA from fecal samples, and performed qPCR with primers specifically recognizing the genomic region of DUF6383 domain-containing protein encoded by P. distasonis. We divided the group into patients with high and low DUF6383 domain-containing protein levels using max-rank selected statistics. We confirmed that patients with high amplification of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had lower 90-day survival (log rank, p = 0.045) (Figure 5A). There was no difference in the MELD score between the two groups, and the genomic DNA of DUF6383 domain-containing proteins was not significantly different in patients with severe vs. non-severe AH (p = 0.85, Figure 5B).

【Validation cohort: · s0002-s2001-s3002-p1】Details of this cohort have been described. 21 We analyzed data and biological samples from 72 individuals enrolled through the Alcoholic Hepatitis Network (AlcHepNet, NCT04072822). Enrollment occurred between May 2019 and May 2022 at eight clinical centers in the United States, including Cleveland Clinic, Indiana University, Mayo Clinic, University of Louisville, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center Boston & University of Massachusetts, University of Pittsburgh, University of Texas Southwestern, and Virginia Commonwealth University.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《DUF6383-domain containing protein from  Parabacteroides distasonis  predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · f0001】Figure 1. Bacterial protein patterns are different in the feces between controls, patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD), and patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH). Characterization of bacterial proteins was performed from fecal samples of controls (Control, n = 19), patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and patients withalcohol-associated hepatitis (AH, InTeam; n = 80). (A) Bacterial proteins in fecal samples in controls, AUD, and AH groups (P = 0.001 PERMANOVA test [ 28 ]; AH vs. AUD P adj. = 0.03, AH vs. healthy P adj. = 0.003, AUD vs. control P adj. = 0.003. P-values were calculated using the dissimilarity index calculated by the method of Bray-Curtis and Permutational Multivariate Analysis of Variance Using Distance Matrices. (B) Protein abundance of the 18 detected proteins, which showed an increase with disease severity and a significant difference between all three groups as calculated by Kruskal–Wallis test, and a significant difference between AH and AUD patients following Wilcoxon rank sum test. P-values for Kruskal–Wallis Test and Wilcoxon rank sum test are listed in Supplemental Table 1. Bif. dentium, Bifidobacterium dentium; B. finegoldii, Bacteroides finegoldii; B. thetaiotaomicron, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron; Bif. bifidum, Bifidobacterium bifidum; C. bolteae, Clostridium bolteae; E. faecium, Enterococcus faecium; Eu. dolichum, Eubacterium dolichum; P. distasonis, Parabacteroides distasonis; R. gnavus, Ruminoccous gnavus; Roseb. inulinivorans, Roseburia inulinivorans; V. atypica, Veillonella atypica; V. parvula, Veillonella parvula; V. seminalis, Veillonella seminalis. (C) A heatmap of bacterial proteins in fecal samples was clustered using hierarchical clustering. The x-axis is the same as the y-axis. P-values were calculated using Pearson correlation. (D) Pearson correlation of the 18 differentially expressed proteins from Figure 1B with histological, clinical, and laboratory parameters. *P < 0.05; **P < 0.01.

【Figure 2. · f0002】Figure 2. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is associated with 90-day mortality and correlates with proteins of neutrophil degranulation in the feces. (A and B) Mallory bodies of patients with AH were divided into low and high groups according to the fecal DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis ((A), P = 0.011) or GTP binding protein level from Dialister spp. ((B), P = 0.024). Optimal cut-off values (cut-off for DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis = 3.325713; cut-off for GTP binding protein from Dialister spp. = 6.507031) were determined using maximally selected rank statistics (maxstat.test in the R package maxstat). P-values were calculated using Wilcoxon-Test. (C) Kaplan‒Meier curve of 90-day mortality for 72 patients with AH (exploratory InTeam cohort). Patients were grouped according to their fecal level of DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis. The cut-off values for the two groups are described in the legend of Figure 2A. The date of liver transplantation was regarded as the death date for patients receiving transplantation (n = 3) and censored patients (n = 3 Log-rank P = 0.0048). (D) Abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P.distasonis in patients with severe AH as defined by a Maddrey score ≥ 32 (n = 51). (E) Abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing proteins from P. distasonis was correlated with 680 human proteins in the feces, which we have described recently 21 using Pearson correlation. Proteins that showed a positive correlation (D, R > 0.2, P < 0.05) were clustered using overrepresentation analysis and Reactome pathways. P-values were adjusted using false-discovery rate.

【Figure 3. · f0003】Figure 3. Taxonomic profiles are different between patients with AH, AUD, and controls. (A–C) The relative abundance of each bacterium was calculated based on the bacterial protein data. (A) Phylum level. Actinobacteria P = 0.00156, Bacteroidetes P = 8.65e-11, Firmicutes P = 8.79e-10, Proteobacteria P = 5.59e-28, Verrucomicrobia P = 0.13. (B) Genus level. Significance Bacteroides P = 1.75 e-6, Blautia P = 0.0781, Clostridium P = 0.000187, Faecalibacterium P = 0.0396, Prevotella P = 3.57e-9, Roseburia P = 0.0274. (C) Species level. Bacteroides dorei P = 0.0106, Bacteroides vulgatus P = 0.0239, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii P = 0.00466, Prevotella copri P = 0.359, Prevotella copri CAG:164 P = 0.485. (D) Relative abundance of P. distasonis. Significance was calculated using Kruskal–Wallis and Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
